title: Accordion Behavior Bug
description:
## Problem Statement

You're a frontend engineer on the CoderX docs team. The FAQ page is built around a reusable `<Accordion>` component (defined in `src/App.jsx`), but the current implementation is broken. It is supposed to behave like a classic **single-open accordion**:

- Every section renders a header `<button>` with class `accordion-trigger`.
- Every section's content panel (class `accordion-panel`) starts **collapsed**.
- Clicking a header **expands** that section's panel.
- Clicking an already-expanded header **collapses** it again.
- Opening one section **auto-closes** any other open section (at most one panel open at a time).
- Each trigger reports the correct `aria-expanded` accessibility state (`"true"` when its own panel is visible, `"false"` otherwise).

All six behaviors above are exercised by the hidden test suite — make them all pass.

### The Fix

Today the accordion never reveals any content — the click handler always collapses the component back to `null`, so every panel stays closed and `aria-expanded` never changes. Rearchitect the state so that it:

1. Tracks **at most one** open index at a time (use `null` to mean "nothing open").
2. **Toggles**: clicking a closed header opens its panel; clicking the already-open header returns the accordion to "nothing open".
3. Drives both panel visibility (the `hidden` attribute on `.accordion-panel`) and the trigger's `aria-expanded` attribute from that single value.

### Notes

- Don't rename `SECTIONS`, the exported `App`, or the `accordion-trigger` / `accordion-panel` class names — the tests rely on them.
- Styling is already provided in `src/App.css` — only fix the behavior, don't change the styles.
- The initial render must keep working (heading + all headers visible, no crash).
